curation.architecture_summary: simple_thinking_tool is a FastMCP server that exposes 15 named thinking methods as individual MCP tools. The core design principle is 'the LLM is the router': the calling agent reads each tool's description and selects the appropriate reasoning mode. The server itself never calls an LLM, makes no outbound network calls, and performs no reasoning — it fills a mode-specific template from caller-provided string fields and appends the rendered note to a durable, append-only JSONL log with fsync. Modes are defined as data in modes.json, so adding or editing a mode requires no code changes. An optional loop guard (off by default) prevents agent churn by blocking same-mode-in-a-row calls and escalating warnings for consecutive think_* calls. Background event hooks allow post-processing automation after notes are stored. The server supports stdio (default) and HTTP transports, with optional bearer-token authentication for HTTP. It is designed as a single-serve private instance — one copy per agent — with no multi-tenancy or shared state. The request lifecycle for a think_* call is: receive tool call → authenticate (resolve actor from bearer token) → validate (guard evaluates anti-churn rules) → render (fill mode template from fields) → persist (append note to JSONL with fsync) → dispatch (fire background hook if configured) → return response to LLM.

clusters.name: Server & Wiring
clusters.rationale: The entry point and configuration layer. server.py wires together all components via build_server(), dynamically generates mode tool functions from modes.json, and registers health/definitions/journal tools. config.py provides environment-driven Settings. __init__.py defines package identity.

clusters.name: Mode System
clusters.rationale: The data-driven thinking mode catalog. modes.json defines 15 modes as data entries; modes.py loads them into frozen Mode dataclasses, renders templates with missing-field tolerance, and exposes definitions for the LLM to read.

clusters.name: Storage Layer
clusters.rationale: The append-only JSONL store with fsync durability, size-based rotation, run_id idempotency, input_hash integrity, and in-memory record caching. Supports both note and session record types.

clusters.name: Security & Identity
clusters.rationale: Token-derived actor identity using constant-time comparison (hmac.compare_digest). Prevents spoofing: actor identity comes from the authenticated bearer token, never from tool input arguments.

clusters.name: Loop Guard
clusters.rationale: Optional anti-churn control (off by default). Evaluates trailing think_* calls per actor: hard-blocks same-mode-in-a-row, escalates warnings at warn_at threshold, hard-blocks at block_at ceiling.

clusters.name: Event Hooks
clusters.rationale: Background fire-and-forget hook dispatch. Resolves mode-specific or generic scripts, writes a minimal JSON payload, runs as a daemon thread subprocess with timeout. Hook failures never break the server.

clusters.name: Service Layer
clusters.rationale: Alternative programmatic API (ThinkingService class) that wraps store, modes, and auth without FastMCP. Does not integrate guard or hooks — appears to be a simpler/earlier interface for direct use.

clusters.name: Test Suite
clusters.rationale: Seven test files covering each module: auth token verification, guard decision logic, hook dispatch, mode loading/rendering, server tool registration, service layer operations, and store append/rotate/idempotency.

critical_paths: think_* call lifecycle: server.py → auth.py (resolve actor) → guard.py (evaluate anti-churn) → modes.py (render template) → store.py (append note with fsync) → hooks.py (fire background hook) → return {ok, mode, modes, note, id, hook?}

inferences.claim: service.py is an alternative or earlier API that predates the guard and hooks integration — it wraps store, modes, and auth but does not invoke the loop guard or fire hooks, suggesting it was the original service layer before server.py added those features.

The store's session management methods (create_session, finalize_session, list_sessions) are not used by the server — the server passes actor_id directly as session_id, treating it as a flat grouping key rather than a session lifecycle, which means session records are never created in normal operation.

The guard's evaluate() method calls store.export() which returns all in-memory records and filters them in Python — for large logs this could become a performance bottleneck since it scans the entire record list on every think_* call.

The server dynamically generates mode functions using exec() with field names from modes.json injected into the generated code — while the field names are operator-controlled (not user input), this pattern requires careful auditing of modes.json to prevent code injection if the file is ever externally modifiable.

The hook runner keeps alive thread references in a list that is filtered on each fire() call — long-running hooks that exceed the timeout will be killed by subprocess timeout, but the daemon thread itself may linger until the process exits.

visual_views.title: Loop Guard Decision Logic
visual_views.purpose: Show the branching decision tree the loop guard uses to determine whether a think_* call is allowed, warned, or hard-blocked.

semantic_nodes.label: think_* called
semantic_nodes.description: A think_<mode> tool is invoked; guard.evaluate() is called with store, actor_id, and mode

semantic_nodes.label: Guard enabled?
semantic_nodes.description: Checks self.enabled flag (set by NUT_THINKING_GUARD_ENABLED=1). If disabled, returns ok immediately.

semantic_nodes.label: Count trailing think_* notes
semantic_nodes.description: Filters store.export() for notes by this actor, counts consecutive trailing notes that have a mode set, includes current call in streak count

semantic_nodes.label: Same mode as last note?
semantic_nodes.description: Checks if the last note's mode matches the current call's mode. If yes and same_mode_block is true, this is pure churn.

semantic_nodes.label: Consecutive >= block_at?
semantic_nodes.description: Checks if consecutive think_* count has reached the hard ceiling (default 5). If yes, hard block until agent produces real work.

semantic_nodes.label: Consecutive >= warn_at?
semantic_nodes.description: Checks if consecutive think_* count has reached the warning threshold (default 3). If yes, allow but inject escalating warning.

semantic_nodes.label: Allow (status: ok)
semantic_nodes.description: GuardResult with allowed=true, status='ok'. The think_* call proceeds normally.

semantic_nodes.label: Allow with warning (status: warn)
semantic_nodes.description: GuardResult with allowed=true, status='warn'. Call proceeds but warning message is returned to the LLM.

semantic_nodes.label: Hard block (status: block)
semantic_nodes.description: GuardResult with allowed=false, status='block'. The think_* call is rejected; block message returned to the LLM.

visual_views.title: JSONL Store Lifecycle
visual_views.purpose: Show the states the JSONL store transitions through during startup, append operations, fsync, and rotation.

semantic_nodes.label: Loading
semantic_nodes.description: On startup, reads existing JSONL file line by line into in-memory _records list. Tolerates partial tail lines (JSONDecodeError skipped).

semantic_nodes.label: Idle
semantic_nodes.description: Store loaded and ready. In-memory records cached. Waiting for append_note or export calls.

semantic_nodes.label: Appending
semantic_nodes.description: Writing a new JSON record as one line to the file. Checks file size for rotation threshold before writing. Acquires threading.Lock.

semantic_nodes.label: Rotating
semantic_nodes.description: File exceeds rotate_bytes (default 5MB). Current file renamed to <stem>.<timestamp>.bak.jsonl. New empty file created for subsequent appends.

semantic_nodes.label: Fsynced
semantic_nodes.description: Line written and os.fsync() called for durability. Record appended to in-memory _records list.

semantic_nodes.label: Closed
semantic_nodes.description: Server shutdown. Store no longer active. No explicit close method — relies on process exit.

semantic_edges.label: rotation complete, write to new file

visual_views.title: Thinking Modes Catalog
visual_views.purpose: Show all 15 thinking modes organized by their difficulty level (1-4), with each mode's typical workflow stage, giving a quick visual overview of the available reasoning methods.

semantic_nodes.label: Thinking Methods
semantic_nodes.description: 15 named reasoning modes auto-registered as MCP tools from modes.json

semantic_nodes.label: Level 1: Core
semantic_nodes.description: Cheapest, most-used modes for everyday reasoning

semantic_nodes.label: Level 2: Structured
semantic_nodes.description: Structured depth modes for moderate-complexity problems

semantic_nodes.label: Level 3: Advanced
semantic_nodes.description: Advanced multi-path and audit modes for complex problems

semantic_nodes.label: Level 4: High-Stakes
semantic_nodes.description: Adversarial and red-team modes for irreversible decisions

semantic_nodes.label: Goal Distillation (plan)
semantic_nodes.description: Reduce turn to one objective, core priority, and first action. Use by default at start of any task.

semantic_nodes.label: Understand / Digest (understand)
semantic_nodes.description: Digest context and content: code, tools, documents, user intents. Use before acting on new material.

semantic_nodes.label: Plan (plan)
semantic_nodes.description: Structure ordered steps before execution with success criteria and blockers.

semantic_nodes.label: Chain of Thought (execute)
semantic_nodes.description: Walk a linear chain of intermediate conclusions from premise to answer.

semantic_nodes.label: Creative / Divergent (any)
semantic_nodes.description: Generate open directions and wildcard ideas without premature selection.

semantic_nodes.label: Deep Think (execute)
semantic_nodes.description: Rephrase, decompose, hypothesize, verify, then synthesize for hard problems.

semantic_nodes.label: Distill / Compress (handoff)
semantic_nodes.description: Compress what survives rephrasing into its essence. Use at handoff or wrap-up.

semantic_nodes.label: Reflect / Socratic (review)
semantic_nodes.description: Socratic self-interrogation: what is actually true here?

semantic_nodes.label: First Principles (any)
semantic_nodes.description: Reduce to fundamental facts and rebuild without inherited assumptions.

semantic_nodes.label: Tree of Thoughts (any)
semantic_nodes.description: Branch multiple paths, score them, prune weak ones, pick a branch.

semantic_nodes.label: Graph of Thoughts (any)
semantic_nodes.description: Build partial solutions as a graph with feedback loops, then aggregate.

semantic_nodes.label: Bias Check (review)
semantic_nodes.description: Scan for confirmation, survivorship, and authority bias before high-stakes calls.

semantic_nodes.label: Metacognitive / Self-Audit (review)
semantic_nodes.description: Audit the reasoning itself for bias, uncertainty, and contradictions.

semantic_nodes.label: Reinforced / Red Team (review)
semantic_nodes.description: Multiple complete takes plus an adversarial red-team attack for high-stakes conclusions.

semantic_nodes.label: Adversarial Review (review)
semantic_nodes.description: Attempt to disprove the provisional conclusion before committing.

visual_views.title: Core Data Schemas
visual_views.purpose: Show the key data structures in the system — Mode, Note record, Session record, GuardResult, Settings, and Hook payload — and their relationships.

semantic_nodes.label: Mode
semantic_nodes.description: Frozen dataclass: id, label, purpose, when, level (1-4), typical_stage, fields (tuple of str), template (str with {field} placeholders), version (int)

semantic_nodes.label: modes.json
semantic_nodes.description: JSON file with a 'modes' array. Each entry has id, label, purpose, when, level, typical_stage, fields, template, version. 15 modes defined.

semantic_nodes.label: Note Record
semantic_nodes.description: JSONL record: type='note', id (ulid-like), session_id, actor_id, parent_thought_id, mode, template_version, note (max 800 chars), next_action, run_id, input_hash (sha256[:16]), ts, meta

semantic_nodes.label: Session Record
semantic_nodes.description: JSONL record: type='session', id, actor_id, project_id, conversation_id, status (open/finalized), created_at, finalized_at. Not used by server in normal operation.

semantic_nodes.label: GuardResult
semantic_nodes.description: Dataclass: allowed (bool), status (ok|warn|block), consecutive (int), last_mode (str|None), message (str). Returned by Guard.evaluate().

semantic_nodes.label: Settings
semantic_nodes.description: 16 env-driven fields: token, boss_token, state_dir, host, port, max_note_chars, burst_limit, transport, actor, allow_modes, rotate_bytes, hooks_dir, hooks_timeout, guard_enabled, guard_same_mode_block, guard_warn_at, guard_block_at

semantic_nodes.label: Hook Payload
semantic_nodes.description: JSON file written to temp dir: {mode, note, actor, ts (ms epoch)}. Passed as file path argument to hook script subprocess. No tokens or secrets.

semantic_edges.label: mode id and template_version stored in note record
session_id links note to session (server uses actor_id as session_id)
guard_enabled, warn_at, block_at configure guard evaluation
note text and mode passed to hook payload
hooks_dir and hooks_timeout configure hook dispatch
